cluster_summary: This cluster contains vulnerabilities where authorization logic is omitted or insufficient, allowing unauthorized access to resources or privilege escalation. The issues span object retrieval (missing filters), field updates (missing privilege checks), privileged actions (missing role checks), and authorization functions (missing return values).
guideline_text: Trace externally reachable requests, RPC messages, management calls, or background command triggers into privileged commands, administrative state changes, credential operations, or protected data access. Report code paths where caller identity is not established before the privileged action begins. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 2 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should require a validated session, principal, token, or authentication filter before any privileged effect.

mechanism.missing_guard: caller identity is not established before the privileged action begins
mechanism.name: missing authentication before privileged action
mechanism.sink_shape: privileged commands, administrative state changes, credential operations, or protected data access
mechanism.source_shape: externally reachable requests, RPC messages, management calls, or background command triggers
mechanism.typical_fix: require a validated session, principal, token, or authentication filter before any privileged effect

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add an explicit return statement (e.g., return 0 or return False) in the else clause of the authorization check to indicate failure.
sub_patterns.name: Missing failure return after authorization check
sub_patterns.root_cause: Authorization functions do not explicitly return a failure value when the check fails, allowing the execution to continue and potentially granting access.

sub_patterns.name: Missing authorization guards in API operations
